  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced in B. Several competitors publish paid prices at or above the hypothesized range: EstimationPro at $66 and $124/mo, Outdoor Estimates at $49.99/mo, and QuoteIQ from $29.99/mo. QuotrPro also cites traction of 500+ contractors and $2.4M+ quoted. For a goal of one paying customer in 90 days, proof that this buyer already pays is the most decision-relevant evidence.",
    "A's pricing ground is being undercut. Of six competitors, Nalvis's engine, BreakShield (in beta), mendapi's CLI and Ripple are free. A's own open questions concede that SMBs may not pay $20-50/mo for what competitors give away. That directly threatens the first paid conversion.",
    "B's buyers pay roughly 2-4x more per month, so each customer is worth more. B's case also includes evidence that single contractor-founders run comparable products.",
    "A has the stronger demand evidence: three sourced quotes against B's single sourced quote, since B's second quote is unsourced and counts as missing. A also has cheaper channels (GitHub Marketplace, community). These are real advantages, but they show pain, not payment.",
    "A carries an extra trust barrier for a solo operator. Granting PR-opening access to source code is trust-sensitive, and spec-diff false-positive rates of about 8x are documented. This likely lengthens time-to-first-payment. B has its own accuracy risk, but the contractor reviews the estimate before sending it.",
    "B's main weaknesses are expensive acquisition ($237 blended CPL, which is generic B2B SaaS rather than contractor-specific) and scope creep from crew scheduling. Its own open questions note the MVP can drop scheduling and ship quoting alone."

  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis of $20-50/mo rests on a single competitor's list price: apidrift.co at $29/mo, with no evidence anyone actually pays it. A's only quantitative acquisition benchmark, the $248 median devtools CAC, comes from a page the brief itself flags as containing a prompt-injection attempt, so it counts only as directional.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. The briefs trade off differently: A has better-sourced demand and cheaper channels, while B has better-sourced willingness to pay at higher price points. Neither brief shows actual conversion rates. I weighted B ahead because the question asks for a paying customer, and A's market shows heavy free competition. A reasonable reviewer who weights channel cost most could pick A."
